source.title: On the birational section conjecture with strong birationality assumptions
source.version: Published open-access PDF, 22 pages, online 26 September 2023; all pp.129–150 reread by codex-hjdg0j on 22 September 2026. arXiv:2108.13397v3 (15 September 2023) checked at the six source-issue passages; its SHA-256 is e23989fbac0cb38646d34a69f8c724611fd1f46a371122197e25f83f18cbb722. All22 published pages reread by codex-c83e7a on2026-09-23; identical published SHA-256. The v3 passage comparison remains attributed to codex-hjdg0j.
readSections: Entire published pp.129–150: introduction, §§2–7, Lemmas1–26, TheoremsA–C, all proofs, footnote1, acknowledgements and references.

summary: Continuation of PR1924: explicit finite-K/Qp Mattuck proof by normalized multiplication iterates on a small analytic ball, including p=2 and arbitrary reduction; compactness/finite torsion and the local Tate-invariant/cocycle steps are separated. Reuses the existing FormalLieTheory and RigidZariskiGeometry candidates. 168 items; original parabolic correctness gap and source/blueprint granularity gaps remain. Partial, no formalization claim.

items.name: Curve and smooth completion
items.statement: A curve is a smooth geometrically connected curve over a characteristic-zero field k; barX is its smooth proper completion. Hyperbolic means 2g(barX)-2+deg(barX\X)>0.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track geometric connectedness, genus, boundary and base change; test P1, Gm, and P1 minus three points.

items.name: Galois section class
items.statement: S_X/k is the set of continuous right inverses of π1(X)→Gal(k), modulo conjugation by π1(X_bar k).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Representatives, quotient invariance, pushforward and base change; test the rational-point section and a tangential section.

items.name: Geometric sections
items.statement: A point x∈X(k) induces a section class by functoriality; a section is geometric when it belongs to this image.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Naturality and conjugacy independence; test X=Spec k and two distinct points on a hyperbolic curve.

items.name: Cuspidal packet
items.statement: For x∈(barX\X)(k), the packet P_X,x is the image of sections of its local decomposition-group extension in S_X/k; a section is cuspidal if it lies in one of these packets.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Use a henselian punctured neighborhood, inertia and tangential splittings; distinguish the cusp from a choice of section in its packet; test the three cusps of P1 minus three points.

items.name: Birational section
items.statement: S_k(X)/k consists of continuous sections Gal(k(X))→Gal(k), modulo geometric-kernel conjugacy. A cuspidal birational section factors through a decomposition group over a k-rational point of barX.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Generic-to-open restriction and packets; a rational point inside X still gives a cuspidal FUNCTION-FIELD section.

items.name: Birationally liftable section
items.statement: A section s∈S_X/k is b.l. precisely when it is in the image S_k(X)/k→S_X/k.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Witness and restriction API; use this definition, which differs from Stix book Definition 266. Do not replace lifting by a local condition.

items.name: t-birationally liftable section
items.statement: A section s∈S_X/k is t-b.l. precisely when s_k(t) is b.l. over the rational-function extension k(t).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Base-change witness and renaming variable; test rational-point and cuspidal sections. Never infer transcendental base change of arbitrary birational sections.

items.name: Section conjecture proposition
items.statement: For every hyperbolic curve over every field finitely generated over Q, every Galois section is geometric or cuspidal.
items.note: Planning API and tests: A named proposition, with no proof assumption in unconditional endpoints; preserve field and hyperbolicity quantifiers.

items.name: Birational section conjecture proposition
items.statement: For every smooth geometrically connected curve over every field finitely generated over Q, every birational section is cuspidal.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Quantify over curves and fields; distinguish the conjecture from the t-b.l. theorem.

items.name: Cuspidalization conjecture proposition
items.statement: For every hyperbolic X over a field finitely generated over Q and every nonempty open U⊆X, the restriction S_U/k→S_X/k is surjective.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Universal open-subset quantifier; test composition of restrictions. This is a conjecture, not an available lifting theorem.

items.name: Nonintegrality places
items.statement: For a birational section z of a smooth projective curve over a number field and nonempty open U with an integral model outside finite S, N_U is the set of places where its associated local point fails to lie in U(O_v).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Model changes alter N_U only by finitely many places; distinguish infinitude, positive Dirichlet density, and density zero.

items.name: Nonintegrality independence
items.statement: The set N_U is independent of the chosen finite-type integral model up to finitely many places; thus its Dirichlet-density question is independent of that model.
items.note: Spread the two models over a common open arithmetic base.

items.name: Stix density alternative
items.statement: For a b.l. section of a hyperbolic curve over a number field, either its associated adelic point is integral on a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one or the section is cuspidal.
items.locator: Published paper §1 p.131; Lemmas 16,20 cite [21] Theorem B
items.note: Read Stix arXiv:1203.3236v3 p.1 Theorem B. Density one does not mean all but finitely many places.

items.name: Stix totally real or imaginary quadratic input
items.statement: For a hyperbolic curve over a totally real or imaginary quadratic number field, every birationally adelic noncuspidal section is geometric.
items.note: Exact source theorem read at Stix p.1. Bresciani’s claim that some N_U is infinite uses this plus deleting an associated rational point; it is not an unconditional all-number-field result.

items.name: Birationally adelic section
items.statement: For a hyperbolic X over a number field with function field K, a section s∈S_X/k is birationally adelic if it has a birational lift z∈S_K/k such that for EVERY nonempty open U⊆X, the induced section on U is either adelic for U/k or cuspidal. An adelic section is a Selmer section whose associated modified adelic point lies in U(A_k)_bullet (integral outside finitely many places, with connected components at infinity).
items.locator: Published paper §1 p.131, input [21] Theorem A
items.note: Planning API and tests: retain existence of ONE birational lift working for all opens and the per-open disjunction; distinguish density-one integrality from adelic integrality. Stix arXiv:1203.3236v3 §2.2.2–§2.2.3 p.4 read.

items.name: Curve family
items.statement: X→V is a family of curves when X=barX\D, barX→V is smooth proper with geometrically connected one-dimensional fibers, and D is a relative divisor finite étale over V.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Base change, empty boundary and fiber; test constant punctured P1 families and a boundary collision that fails étaleness.

items.name: Relative π1 section
items.statement: For a family X→V over an affine curve, a π1 section is a continuous splitting π1(V)→π1(X), modulo conjugation by the geometric-fiber group.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Specialization at v∈V(k), conjugacy independence and shrinking V; test a constant section of a product.

items.name: Profinite completion of an abelian group
items.statement: For abelian A, Ahat=lim over positive n of A/nA, with transition maps for divisibility. For multiplicative groups use A/A^n.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Projection, induced maps, separatedness hypotheses and compatibility with valuation; compare Zhat and completion of k*. Infinite direct sums do not become unrestricted products.

items.name: fpqc and fppf sites
items.statement: The fpqc topology is generated by jointly surjective quasi-compact flat covering families; fppf uses flat locally finitely presented covers.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Use existing sites and inclusion; test fppf≤fpqc. Do not construct new sites for torsors.

items.name: Stack descent framework
items.statement: A category-valued pseudofunctor on a site is a stack if it is a prestack and descent data for covering sieves are effective.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Reuse IsStack and effective descent equivalence; test a trivial cover. This does not claim a geometric gerbe implementation.

items.name: Finite and profinite étale gerbes
items.statement: A finite étale gerbe over k is an étale gerbe with finite geometric automorphism groups; a profinite étale gerbe is a cofiltered 2-limit of such gerbes.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Isomorphism groupoids, neutralizations, band and finite-stage presentation; test BG for a finite constant group and inverse limits.

items.name: Classifying stack of a group scheme
items.statement: B_kG assigns to a k-scheme S the groupoid of fpqc G_S-torsors. For finite-type G the fppf topology suffices; retain fpqc for profinite G.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Pullback, trivial torsor, automorphism group, equivalence under group-scheme isomorphism; test μ_n and Zhat(1).

items.name: Étale fundamental gerbe
items.statement: For the geometrically connected schemes in the paper, X→Π_X/k is universal for maps from X to finite étale stacks, and Π_X/k is a profinite étale gerbe.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Universal equivalence on Hom groupoids, functoriality, comparison to IG.0’s finite-cover fiber functor; test Spec k, A1 and Gm.

items.name: Sections as gerbe points
items.statement: The isomorphism classes of Π_X/k(k) identify with S_X/k, compatibly with rational points, functoriality and conjugacy.
items.note: Use the actual groupoid comparison, not equality of bare cardinalities.

items.name: Pointed fundamental group scheme
items.statement: Given x∈X(k), descend the continuous Gal(k)-action on π1(X_bar k,x) to an étale profinite group scheme π1(X,x). There is a neutralization Π_X/k≃B_kπ1(X,x).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track choice of x and twisting by its torsor; test trivial torsor and a change of rational point.

items.name: Fundamental gerbe base change
items.statement: In characteristic zero, for a geometrically connected concentrated fibered category X and any extension k′/k, Π_(X_k′)/k′≃Π_X/k×k k′. In particular this applies to the paper’s curves and k(t).
items.locator: Published paper §2 p.133 and p.135, citation [6] A.18
items.note: CORRECTED LOCATOR: [6] published Proposition A.23, p.264, read; A.18 p.262 only proves algebraic separable extensions. Concentration and char 0 are retained.

items.name: Family homotopy exact sequence
items.statement: Let k have characteristic zero, A be a localization of a one-dimensional regular finite-type k-domain, C=Spec A, and X→C a family of curves. For a geometric fiber F, 1→π1(F)→π1(X)→π1(C)→1 is exact.
items.note: Proof uses complex affine-curve π2=0, exactness of profinite completion for the specified curve groups, descent to C, and limits of finite étale covers. Do not generalize to arbitrary proper bases.

items.name: Complex affine-curve asphericity input
items.statement: A smooth connected affine complex curve has the homotopy type of a finite wedge of circles, hence π2=0 and finitely generated free π1. For a locally trivial topological curve family over it, the homotopy sequence is short exact on π1; the fiber group is finitely generated.
items.note: The curve-topology/Riemann-existence and locally trivial family comparisons remain IG.1 proof obligations. Completion now uses /29 and /140–/145, not the unread Anderson theorem or cohomological goodness. A group-theoretic splitting does not assert a geometric section of the family.

items.name: Completion exactness input for curve families
items.statement: For the complex affine-base topological curve-family extension 1→N→G→F_r→1 in Lemma1, N is finitely generated and F_r is free; therefore 1→hat N→hat G→hat F_r→1 is split exact as profinite groups.
items.locator: Published Lemma1 p.134; replacement proof in this continuation, using /140–/145; independently Bekka, arXiv:2305.04803v1, CorollaryC p.4.
items.note: CLOSED SOURCE GAP BY REPLACEMENT, not a claim to have read Anderson. Lift free generators to split the abstract extension; characteristic finite-index subgroups of N provide cofinal finite quotient restrictions from G. The completion universal property gives right exactness and extends the splitting. No residual-finiteness or goodness assumption is needed; finite generation of N and splitting are essential to this proof. Generic completion lemma belongs only to ProfiniteProPGroupsPartIISplitCompletion; IG.1 owns this geometric application.

items.name: Limit of finite étale covers
items.statement: For C a localization of a finite-type regular affine curve, finite étale covers descend to an open neighborhood U, giving π1(C)≃lim_U π1(U); the analogous assertion holds for the spread-out family.
items.note: Record filtered descent and eventual equality of morphisms; constant left term identifies the inverse-limit extension.

items.name: Relative fundamental gerbe
items.statement: Π_X/C is the 2-fiber product C×_(Π_C/k)Π_X/k, with its natural map X→Π_X/C over C.
items.note: Planning API and tests: 2-cartesian universal property, sections and base change; test constant families.

items.name: Relative fiber comparison
items.statement: Under Lemma 1 hypotheses, for every field extension k′/k and c:Spec k′→C, Π_(X_c)/k′→Π_X/C×_C Spec k′ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Requires /26’s arbitrary-extension base change and /27’s full exactness, not just right exactness.

items.name: Proper étale relative-gerbe presentation
items.statement: Π_X/C→C is a cofiltered limit of proper étale relative gerbes Φ_i→C.
items.note: Present source and target by finite étale gerbes with locally full transition maps and set Φ_i=Ψ_i×_(Ξ_i)C.

items.name: Locally full morphism of gerbes
items.statement: For affine gerbes over k, a morphism is locally full when the induced automorphism-group map at every field-valued object is faithfully flat; equivalently the maps of fpqc Isom sheaves are surjective. On neutral finite étale geometric fibers this is surjectivity of finite band groups.
items.note: Definition3.4 and Proposition3.10 read directly, published pp.538–540. Planning API/tests: composition, fpqc base change and neutral BG→BH comparison; test a surjection, a proper subgroup inclusion and identity. Scheme-theoretic faithful flatness is primary, not surjectivity on k-rational points.

items.name: Locally full finite étale gerbes are relative gerbes
items.statement: A locally full morphism of finite étale gerbes over k is a proper étale relative gerbe.
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma2 p.135; Borne–Vistoli2019 Proposition3.10 pp.540–541.
items.note: Exact affine-gerbe criterion read: locally full iff relative gerbe. For finite étale gerbes, after an fpqc neutralizing cover the fiber is B ker(G→H), with finite étale kernel, hence proper and étale; descend those properties. Presentation by locally full projections is split into /149 rather than bundled here. The proof text of Prop3.10 mislabels its factorization implications as (1)⇒(3)/(3)⇒(1); their argument concerns condition(4), not a change of theorem.

items.name: Finite root stack of a DVR
items.statement: For DVR R with uniformizer π, the nth root stack of its closed divisor classifies triples (L,s,α:L^n≃O) with α(s^n)=π; it is [Spec R[t]/(t^n−π)/μ_n].
items.note: Planning API and tests: Prove independence of uniformizer, transition maps when n divides m, generic isomorphism and reduced closed fiber Bμ_n. Test n=1.

items.name: Infinite root stack and specializing circle
items.statement: The infinite root stack is lim_n root_n(Spec R). Its reduced closed fiber S_c^1 is noncanonically B_k Zhat(1); its k-point isomorphism classes are noncanonically H1(k,Zhat(1))=completed k*.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Distinguish stack from set of isomorphism classes and choice-free object from chosen neutralization; test a change of uniformizer.

items.name: Constant gerbe morphism
items.statement: A morphism Y→X of fibered categories over k is constant if it factors through Spec k.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Factorization witnesses and invariance under equivalence; test a trivial group homomorphism and a nontrivial map Bμ_n→Bμ_n.

items.name: Tame stack valuative input
items.statement: For a tame proper morphism of algebraic stacks X→Y, a DVR R with fraction field K, and a compatible generic lift Spec K→X over Spec R→Y, there is a unique positive n and a representable lift root_n(Spec R)→X; the lift is unique up to a unique compatible isomorphism.
items.note: Primary arXiv:2210.03406v1 pp.3–4 read. The representability condition is essential for uniqueness of n; no residue-field extension is needed.

items.name: Extension to infinite root stack
items.statement: For the curve family and closed point of Proposition 3, a generic section z extends uniquely up to a unique compatible isomorphism from Spec K to the infinite root stack of the local DVR.
items.note: Apply the proper tame criterion at each finite gerbe stage and pass to the limit; uniqueness is relative to the specified generic datum.

items.name: Specializing loop
items.statement: The specializing loop γ_z(c):S_c^1→Π_(X_c)/k(c) is the restriction of the infinite-root-stack extension of z to the reduced closed fiber.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Functoriality, finite-level compatibility and base change; test Gm and valuation-zero versus nonzero sections.

items.name: Unramified extension criterion
items.statement: The generic section extends over Spec R if and only if its specializing loop is constant.
items.note: Retain R and the relative gerbe from the proposition; use the fixed generic datum in uniqueness.

items.name: Possibly nonunique specialization
items.statement: A specialization of z at c is a section class in the essential image of γ_z(c) evaluated on k(c)-points.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Existence, pushforward and field-base-change compatibility; specialize the chosen trivial torsor after a neutralization.

items.name: Existence and one-way uniqueness
items.statement: Specializations always exist. If the specializing loop is constant then the specialization is unique.
items.note: Split from the false converse; existence uses rational points of S_c^1 after a uniformizer choice.

items.name: Automorphism criterion for constancy
items.statement: For a chosen s∈S_c^1(k(c)), γ_z(c) is constant iff Aut(s)=Zhat(1)→Aut(γ_z(c)(s)) is trivial. Consequently constancy can be checked after algebraic closure of the constant field.
items.note: Retain descent compatibility; triviality of geometric band map is stronger than cardinality-one image on rational points.

items.name: Henselian specialization by a uniformizer
items.statement: Choose compatible roots of a uniformizer in the henselization R^h. They split Gal(K^h)→Gal(k), and composing that splitting with a generic section and specialization π1(X_Rh)≃π1(X_k) yields a specialization.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track root choices, decomposition subgroup and inertia I≃Zhat(1); recover the gerbe construction. Characteristic zero of both fields excludes wild inertia here.

items.name: Ramification map and nonabelian H1 image
items.statement: A chosen specialization makes I→π1(X_bar k) Galois equivariant; the set of specializations is its image on nonabelian Galois H1. An unramified section has trivial ramification map.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Twisting action, conjugacy independence and map on torsors; compare constant-loop and unramified notions without assuming injectivity of H1 maps.

items.name: Gm fundamental gerbe and Kummer description
items.statement: The section 1 identifies Π_Gm/R with B_R Zhat(1); its R- and K-point classes are completed R* and completed K* respectively.
items.note: The compact-coefficient Kummer comparison and torsor interpretation are explicit missing adapters.

items.name: Completed valuation
items.statement: A DVR valuation v:K*→Z induces v:completed K*→Zhat. Its kernel is the image of completed R*; the split decomposition K*=R*×π^Z gives the proof.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Evaluation on a uniformizer, compatibility with ramification index and independence of the splitting for v; test v(π)=1.

items.name: Gm loop criterion
items.statement: For a generic Gm section z∈completed K*, its specializing loop is constant iff v(z)=0.
items.note: Uses completed valuation and the extension criterion; no positive-characteristic assertion.

items.name: Unique specialization does not imply constant loop
items.statement: For R=C[x]_(x), the generic Gm section represented by x has nonconstant loop because v(x)=1, but has a unique specialization because H1(C,Zhat(1)) is trivial.
items.note: Required negative unit test for the specialization API.

items.name: Finite local image forces a constant torus loop
items.statement: Let T/k be a torus and ν:k*→Z a surjective valuation. If γ:B_k Zhat(1)→Π_T/k has finitely many isomorphism classes in the image on kν-points of its k-points, then γ is constant.
items.note: Split T over a finite extension k′; the completed valuation surjects onto Zhat. Ramification index r≠0 and torsion-freeness force rf=0⇒f=0.

items.name: Finite local image forces a constant curve loop
items.statement: Let k be a number field, ν a finite place, X/k a curve. If γ:B_k Zhat(1)→Π_X/k has finite image on kν-isomorphism classes of its k-points, then γ is constant.
items.note: Pass to finite étale cover detecting nontriviality in abelianization; use generalized Jacobian, weight separation, Mattuck and Lemma 7.

items.name: Finite-cover abelian detection
items.statement: Let 1→G→E→G_k→1 be the arithmetic fundamental-group sequence of a smooth geometrically connected curve X/k in characteristic zero, s:G_k→E a section, and f:Zhat(1)→G a nontrivial continuous homomorphism equivariant for s. There is an open subgroup E′⊂E containing s(G_k) and f(Zhat(1)), projecting onto G_k, such that f is nonzero in (E′∩G)^ab. Thus the corresponding geometrically connected finite étale cover Y→X has a lift of s and of the loop, with nonconstant abelianized loop.
items.note: Choose a characteristic open subgroup N⊂G detecting f, using finite generation of the geometric curve group. In G/N the image C of f is cyclic and s(G_k)-stable. Let H be its inverse image and E′=H⋊s(G_k). Then H→C is an abelian quotient detecting f. The finite-fiber map on section classes preserves the finite local-image condition. This makes the arithmetic descent and the neutralizing object explicit; no rational point is chosen.

items.name: Finite fibers under finite étale covers
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism Y→X, the map of section classes has finite fibers, so finite-image conditions survive passage to a suitable section neighborhood.
items.note: Use cosets of the finite-index fundamental subgroup; isolate any finite constant-field extension needed.

items.name: Semiabelian Jacobian and Albanese torsor
items.statement: For a smooth open curve X with completion and reduced boundary, construct its generalized Jacobian J, an extension 1→T→J→A→1 with A the proper Jacobian, together with the degree-one Albanese torsor when no rational base point is given.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Keep torsor and group distinct; test proper curves T=0, Gm with J=Gm, and a curve without a rational point.

items.name: Tate module of a semiabelian variety
items.statement: For J as above, TJ=lim_n J[n] on geometric points with its profinite Galois action; 0→TT→TJ→TA→0 is the torsion-limit extension.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Compare all-prime and primewise modules, base change, exactness and π1(J_bar k); test Gm giving Zhat(1).

items.name: Abelianized fundamental gerbe comparison
items.statement: Let X/k be a smooth geometrically connected curve in characteristic zero, J its generalized Jacobian and P its generalized Albanese torsor, with a:X→P. The induced map Π_X/k^ab→Π_P/k is an equivalence of gerbes banded by TJ. Given s∈Π_X/k(k), its images s_ab and a(s) neutralize these gerbes, giving (Π_X/k^ab,s_ab)≃(B_k TJ,*)≃(Π_P/k,a(s)). In particular the loop γ:B_k Zhat(1)→Π_X/k of Lemma 8, with s=γ(*), induces a Galois-equivariant homomorphism Zhat(1)→TJ. Neither X(k) nor P(k) is assumed nonempty.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 8 p.138; Harari–Szamuely, author bash5.pdf, §1 and Remark 2.4; Bresciani 1904.00789v2, Lemma 5.8
items.note: Comparison resolved from /150 (geometric isomorphism), /151 (canonical band of a semiabelian torsor), and /152 (neutralization by a chosen gerbe object). Equivalence is checked after separable base change; commutativity makes the band descent independent of translations. The section does not trivialize P as a J-torsor. This repairs the missing choice in the printed canonical identification; see sourceIssue E4 and the report. Routed once to JacobianChallengePartIIGeneralizedAlbanese.

items.name: Weight vanishing for abelian Tate modules
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field, every Galois-equivariant homomorphism Zhat(1)→TA is zero.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 8 p.138; input [7] Lemma 3.3 read
items.note: Use primewise weight −2 versus −1 at good finite places and injectivity into rational Tate modules; import actual purity results, not merely a weight label.

items.name: Abelian variety carrier
items.statement: An abelian variety is a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field; smoothness and commutativity are derived in the pinned implementation.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Reuse carrier, zero, multiplication and base change; test the zero object and an elliptic curve.

items.name: Abelian Tate modules and torsion
items.statement: Construct A[n] and T_l A as the compatible torsion system, with Galois action and functoriality.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Do not replace torsion group schemes in characteristic p by geometric points; here the base field has characteristic zero.

items.name: Mattuck finite torsion input
items.statement: If K is a finite extension of Q_p and A/K is an abelian variety, A(K) has an open subgroup isomorphic as a topological group to the additive group O_K^dim A; in particular A(K)_tors is finite.
items.note: The finite-K/Qp endpoint now has the explicit small-ball proof /153–/166. Projectivity and generic analytic-coordinate/series suppliers are recorded separately; no full recursive closure is claimed. The original complete-ultrametric-field theorem is broader and is not substituted for this stated finite-extension scope.
proofSteps: Use /164 for the open subgroup U≃O_K^g.
By /166 and /165, A(K) is compact. Its open cosets form a cover, so a finite subcover gives finite index.

items.name: Vanishing inverse torsion and H1 injection
items.statement: For 0→TT→TJ→TA→0 over a p-adic local field, finite torsion of A(K) implies lim_n A[n](K)=0, hence H1(K,TT)→H1(K,TJ) is injective.
items.note: Expanded by /167 and /168: a common exponent kills every compatible inverse-limit component, followed by an explicit coboundary argument.

items.name: Étale divisor through a closed special-fiber point
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero DVR R, a curve family X/R and a closed point p∈X_k, there exists a nonempty divisor D⊂X, finite étale over R, containing p.
items.note: Proof: generic projection of a projective completion avoiding boundary and ramification at geometric points over p; reduce to P1, lift the minimal separable polynomial and choose an unramified section. No henselian assumption.

items.name: Projection used to build the étale divisor
items.statement: Choose a codimension-two linear center disjoint from barX_k, transverse hyperplane fibers through all geometric points over p and avoiding the boundary. Lift its two linear equations to R to get a finite morphism barX→P1_R, étale over a neighborhood of the image of p.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track properness, regularity, flatness and purity of branch locus; test non-rational p as well as rational p.

items.name: Separable residue polynomial lifting
items.statement: A monic lift q∈R[t] of a monic separable irreducible qbar∈k[t] defines a finite étale local R-algebra R′=R[t]/q whose residue field is k[t]/qbar; R′ is a DVR.
items.note: Choose a monic lift with the same degree. Unit discriminant gives étaleness, and irreducible reduction plus finiteness gives a local ring, hence a DVR. An arbitrary lift is insufficient: for R=Q[u]_(u), qbar=T and q=uT²+T, R[T]/q≃R×Q(u), which is not finite over R. See sourceIssue E5.

items.name: Cofinal étale boundary divisors
items.statement: For a curve family X/R there is a directed system of finite étale divisors D_i such that the complement of their union in X_k consists only of the generic point.
items.note: Apply Lemma9 successively to the family with the PREVIOUS finite étale divisor removed, so new divisors are disjoint from earlier ones; a finite disjoint union remains finite étale. Arbitrary finite unions of intersecting étale divisors need not be étale. The resulting limit of opens has closed fiber Spec k(X_k).

items.name: Specialization preserves birational lifting
items.statement: Every specialization of a b.l. generic section of a characteristic-zero DVR curve family is b.l.
items.note: Lift through the inverse system X\D_i and its specializing loops to the function field of the closed fiber.

items.name: t-b.l. implies b.l.
items.statement: Every t-b.l. section of a curve over a characteristic-zero field is b.l.
items.note: Use R=k[t]_(t) and Lemma 11; no claim of the converse.

items.name: Specialization preserves t-birational lifting
items.statement: Every specialization of a t-b.l. generic section is t-b.l.
items.note: Use the DVR at the generic point of A1_k⊂A1_R, with fraction K(t) and residue k(t), then Lemma 11.

items.name: Dominant pushforward preserves b.l.
items.statement: For a dominant map of curves f:Y→X, a b.l. section s of Y has b.l. image f(s).
items.note: Induced inclusion of function fields and section restriction.

items.name: Finite étale pullback detects b.l.
items.statement: For finite étale f:Y→X and a section s of Y, if f(s) is b.l., then s is b.l.
items.note: Use Gal(k(Y))=π1(Y)×_(π1(X))Gal(k(X)); this does not say that every X-section lifts to Y.

items.name: Dominant pushforward preserves t-b.l.
items.statement: For dominant f:Y→X, a t-b.l. section of Y has t-b.l. image.
items.note: Base change Lemma 14 to k(t).

items.name: Finite étale pullback detects t-b.l.
items.statement: For finite étale f:Y→X and a section s of Y, f(s) t-b.l. implies s t-b.l.
items.note: Base change and fiber-product Galois identity; requires a section already on Y.

items.name: Parabolic curve
items.statement: X is parabolic when barX has genus zero and deg(barX\X)≤2.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Boundary degree over k, not number of k-rational punctures; test P1, A1, Gm and a nonsplit degree-two boundary.

items.name: Proper genus-zero sections
items.statement: For a proper genus-zero curve X there is a unique section class, and it is geometric iff X≃P1 over k.
items.note: The unique abstract section need not be geometric for a nonsplit conic; use as a negative test.

items.name: Nonsplit-boundary counterexample to blanket cuspidality
items.statement: Let X=P1_Q minus the closed point V(T²−2). Then X is affine parabolic, X(Q) contains 0, and the boundary has no Q-rational point. Thus X admits geometric sections but no cuspidal section under Bresciani §1's definition. Consequently the printed p.141 assertion that every affine-parabolic section is cuspidal is false.
items.note: This valid counterexample, not the false source sentence, is the item routed as a negative acceptance theorem to the birational-sections Part II. It does not refute TheoremA. The nonsplit degree-two-boundary branches of /81 and /96 remain a genuine proof-repair gap; routing this counterexample does not close that gap.

items.name: Local points of b.l. sections
items.statement: For a curve over a number field and a b.l. section s, at every finite place ν there is xν∈barX(kν) inducing its local geometric or cuspidal section; for nonparabolic X, xν is unique.
items.locator: Published paper §4 p.141, Koenigsmann [13], Stix [21] Proposition 1
items.note: Separate existence from uniqueness in design; do not claim this supplies a global rational point.

items.name: p-adic birational section theorem input
items.statement: For a finite extension K/Q_p and a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X/K, a section Gal(K(X))→Gal(K) comes from a K-rational valuation point.
items.note: Koenigsmann original theorem is a prerequisite for the local existence assertion; no claim that ordinary sections of arbitrary p-adic curves are all geometric.

items.name: Local point-section injectivity
items.statement: For a smooth proper curve of positive genus over a p-adic local field, its rational-point-to-section map is injective; passing to an étale neighborhood yields uniqueness of the local point in the nonparabolic case.
items.note: The genus restriction matters; P1 is the counterexample.

items.name: Lifting t-b.l. sections to opens over number fields
items.statement: For a curve X over a number field, nonempty open U⊆X and t-b.l. section s, there is a t-b.l. section of U mapping to s.
items.note: Begin with a b.l. lift over k(t), use Stix density and Lemma 8 at every closed point, extend over A1 and descend along Π_A1/k=Spec k. The printed blanket parabolic reduction has the explicit /77 counterexample; the general-curve proof remains a checkpoint gap until that branch is repaired.

items.name: Density-one places intersect a splitting condition
items.statement: For a number field extension k′/k, finite places ν admitting an embedding k′→kν have positive Dirichlet density; hence such a ν can be chosen in any density-one set.
items.note: Use completely split primes of a Galois closure, via upstream Chebotarev; no new density theorem here.

items.name: Local-to-global extension of a profinite gerbe map
items.statement: For a normal curve V/k and a profinite étale gerbe Φ/k, if a map Spec k(V)→Φ extends to Spec O_V,v at every closed point, it extends over V, uniquely relative to the generic map.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 16 p.142 and Theorem C p.149, [5] Corollary A.3
items.note: Read [5] arXiv:1904.00789v2 p.27: A.3 requires stabilization of maximal opens. Here every finite-stage maximal open is all V by A.2(ii), so that condition is proved.

items.name: Fundamental gerbe of the affine line
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field k, Π_A1/k≃Spec k, so maps A1→a profinite étale gerbe factor through a k-section.
items.note: Use geometric simple connectedness and the rational point; do not transport to characteristic p.

items.name: Diagonal puncture and pro-open curve
items.statement: Let δ:Spec k(t)→A1_k be the generic point considered over k(t). The pro-open scheme Spec k(A1)×_k Spec k(t) with its diagonal point deleted is the limit of U_k(t)\{δ} over nonempty k-opens U⊆A1.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Distinguish k(y)⊗k k(t) from the field k(t)(y); deleting δ is meaningful before passing to the total function field.

items.name: Rationality from a diagonal-deleted lift
items.statement: Let k be a number field, ν finite, U=A1\{1,2}, s a b.l. section, and xν its associated local point. If s_k(t) lifts to a section of Spec k(A1)×_k Spec k(t)\{δ}, then xν∈P1(k).
items.note: The hypothesis is implied by t-b.l.; retain the stronger-than-an-open-lift pro-open object.

items.name: Diagonal-family specializations lift birationally
items.statement: For the lift r in Proposition 17 and any c∈U(k) distinct from xν, every specialization r_c on U\{c} is b.l. and maps to s.
items.note: Use W=(Spec O_c×_k Spec O_c)\Δ as a projective limit of curve families, with closed fiber Spec k(t).

items.name: Constancy away from the local point
items.statement: For such c, the local image of every specialization r_c is the same point xν; Lemma 8 forces the specializing loop at c to be constant. The argument persists after every finite constant-field extension.
items.note: Exclude c=xν and all boundary points; this controls non-rational closed points after finite extension.

items.name: Moving-coordinate Kummer section
items.statement: The automorphism y↦t−y sends δ to zero and transports r to a section on A1_k(t)\{0,t−1,t−2}; its Gm image is z∈completed k(t)*.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Evaluation at a specialization gives c−xη; test the signs and images of 1,2,δ.

items.name: Restricted completed factorization
items.statement: Every z∈completed k(t)* has unique data λ∈completed k* and exponents e_c∈Zhat at monic irreducible q_c, with for every n only finitely many e_c nonzero modulo n, and z=λ∏q_c^e_c.
items.locator: Published paper Proposition 17 p.143 and footnote 1
items.note: The completion embeds in, but is not the entire unrestricted product. Constant exponent 1 at every c is a negative test; derive from k(t)*≃k*×⊕_c Z.

items.name: Support of the moving-coordinate section
items.statement: For the z of Proposition 17, all e_c vanish except at 1,2 and (if algebraic) the closed point of xν. Thus z=λ q^e(t−1)^e1(t−2)^e2, taking q=1,e=0 when xν is transcendental.
items.note: Uses the Gm valuation criterion after finite extensions; q is the monic minimal polynomial, not a polynomial for an arbitrary completion point.

items.name: Specialization valuation identity
items.statement: Over a finite K/k splitting q and a place η above ν, for c∈K excluding 1,2 and roots of q, λ q(c)^e(c−1)^e1(c−2)^e2=c−xη in completed Kη*. Hence η(λ)+eη(q(c))−η(c−xη)+e1η(c−1)+e2η(c−2)=0 in Zhat.
items.note: Respect completion-valued λ and the chosen extension of local points.

items.name: Elimination of boundary exponents
items.statement: Applying the valuation identity along K-points approaching 1 and 2, with all other factors nonzero there, gives e1=e2=0.
items.note: Differences of unbounded integral valuations are nonzero integers; multiplication by any such integer is injective on Zhat.

items.name: Algebraicity and degree-one conclusion
items.statement: With e1=e2=0, density of K in Kη rules out q=1. Approaching xη forces e=1; approaching another distinct root of separable q contradicts the identity. Thus deg q=1.
items.note: Characteristic zero supplies separability; approaching a transcendental local point is valid even though that point is not in K.

items.name: Quasi-t-birational lifting
items.statement: A section s of X is quasi-t-b.l. if some nonempty open U⊆X has a b.l. lift s′ and a dominant map U→Y to a nonparabolic curve such that the image of s′ is t-b.l.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Store all witnesses; transport under dominant maps only with valid nonparabolic target witnesses; test t-b.l. nonparabolic curves via identity.

items.name: t-b.l. sections are quasi-t-b.l.
items.statement: Every t-b.l. section is quasi-t-b.l., using the nonparabolic reduction when needed.
items.note: Do not use the identity map to a parabolic target; the special parabolic cases must be discharged. The printed blanket parabolic reduction has the explicit /77 counterexample; the general-curve proof remains a checkpoint gap until that branch is repaired.

items.name: Open lifting for quasi-t-b.l. sections
items.statement: A quasi-t-b.l. section lifts to a quasi-t-b.l. section of every nonempty open subset.
items.note: Restrict the birational witness and the dominant map; no number-field assumption needed.

items.name: Specialization after shrinking for quasi-t-b.l. sections
items.statement: For C a curve, a family X→C and a quasi-t-b.l. generic section, there is a nonempty open U⊆C such that all specializations over U are quasi-t-b.l.
items.note: Spread the witnessing nonparabolic family and quasi-finite map, then use Lemmas 11 and 13.

items.name: Number-field quasi-t reduction
items.statement: If every t-b.l. section of every curve over a fixed number field k is geometric or cuspidal, then the same holds for quasi-t-b.l. sections over k.
items.note: The common image point y on the target forces local points into f^-1(y); apply Stix to a b.l. lift on the complement.

items.name: Tamagawa empty-point neighborhood
items.statement: For hyperbolic X/k with k finitely generated over Q, a section neither geometric nor cuspidal lifts to a finite étale Y→X with genus≥2 and barY(k)=∅.
items.note: Keep the statement as printed; original Tamagawa proof and exact compactness/finiteness leaves remain a named prerequisite.

items.name: Reduction from finitely generated fields to number fields
items.statement: If t-b.l. sections over all number fields are geometric or cuspidal, then quasi-t-b.l. sections over all fields finitely generated over Q are geometric or cuspidal.
items.note: Induct on transcendence degree; use a finite cover mapping to a constant elliptic curve, finite-extension descent, generic section extension, and coherence.

items.name: Finite cover mapping to a constant elliptic curve
items.statement: For a smooth projective curve X/k and an elliptic curve E over a subfield h, finite maps X→P1 and E_k→P1 yield, after selecting a component and a finite constant extension, a smooth finite cover Y→X with a finite map Y→E_k.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Normalize fiber product, shrink to an étale map for lifting, track geometric connectedness after extension; test a constant X.

items.name: Fundamental full faithfulness
items.statement: A variety/DM stack is fundamentally fully faithful when its rational-point functor to its fundamental gerbe is fully faithful over every finitely generated field extension in the cited convention.
items.locator: Published paper Proposition 22 input [6] Lemma 6.5 and Theorem 7.2
items.note: Planning API and tests: Record quantifiers and centralizer triviality, not just injectivity on isomorphism classes. Proper genus≥2 curves satisfy the needed form.

items.name: Descent of geometric sections
items.statement: For a separated fundamentally fully faithful finite-type DM stack in the characteristic-zero setting of [6], if a k-section becomes geometric over a finitely generated extension k′/k, it is geometric over k.
items.note: Published [6] p.244 and arXiv pp.14–15 read; for the application X is a smooth proper genus≥2 curve. Do not assume the section conjecture to get fundamental full faithfulness.

items.name: Fundamental full faithfulness for proper curves
items.statement: Smooth proper curves of genus at least one over fields finitely generated over Q satisfy the fundamental-full-faithfulness assertion used in [6] Theorem 7.2; in particular genus≥2 curves do.
items.note: Read theorem’s proper-orbicurve χ≤0 criterion at published p.245. The extraction uses only the scheme case.

items.name: Generic section extension for projective families
items.statement: Let C be affine over a field finitely generated over Q and X→C smooth projective with geometrically connected fibers whose geometric π1 has no abelian torsion. Every generic section extends uniquely over C.
items.note: [7] arXiv:1911.03234v3 p.7 read. Every open subgroup must have torsion-free abelianization; this is true for smooth projective curves, not a consequence of abstract profiniteness.

items.name: No abelian torsion
items.statement: A profinite group G has no abelian torsion when for every open subgroup H⊆G the abelianization H^ab is torsion-free.
items.locator: Published paper Proposition 22 input [7] Definition 3.1 p.7
items.note: Planning API and tests: Closed/open subgroup distinction; test geometric fundamental groups of smooth projective curves via Jacobians, and a finite cyclic counterexample.

items.name: Coherence of a curve family
items.statement: A family X→C is coherent if every pointwise geometric quasi-section over a quasi-finite curve C′→C has geometric generic fiber; pointwise means at every point over every finite constant-field extension.
items.locator: Published paper Proposition 22 input [7] Definition 4.1 pp.7–8
items.note: Planning API and tests: Base change of quasi-sections and all finite-extension specializations; checking only C(k) is insufficient.

items.name: Coherence from a constant abelian target
items.statement: A smooth proper genus≥2 curve family over an affine curve C/h, with h finitely generated over Q, is coherent if its generic fiber has a nonconstant map to an abelian variety defined over h.
items.locator: Published paper Proposition 22 input [7] Corollary 4.9 p.10
items.note: Read [7] pp.7–10 including Prop4.6 and Lemmas4.7–4.8. This special case uses Faltings and Hilbert irreducibility; it does not invoke the conditional Bombieri–Lang branch.

items.name: Faltings Tate-module comparison input
items.statement: For abelian varieties over a field finitely generated over Q, the primewise Tate-module realization identifies Hom(A,B)⊗Z_l with Galois-equivariant Hom(T_l A,T_l B); its all-prime completion supplies the Hom used in the coherence proof.
items.locator: Published paper Proposition 22 input [7] Proposition 4.6 p.9
items.note: [7] Proposition4.6 uses INTEGRAL/all-prime completed Hom over a finitely generated field. R28.4 explicitly plans the rational Q_l comparison; it is not evidence that the integral statement is already planned. Add the saturation/integral comparison and the finitely-generated-field version as named source obligations in that same Tate-isogeny layer, with A3 torsion and specialization inputs.

items.name: Theorem A forward direction
items.statement: For every smooth geometrically connected curve X over k finitely generated over Q, every geometric or cuspidal section is t-b.l.
items.note: Use local decomposition splittings and base change; include the proper genus-zero branch.

items.name: Theorem A reverse direction
items.statement: For every such X/k, every t-b.l. section is geometric or cuspidal.
items.note: Reduce to number fields via Proposition22, apply Tamagawa, lift to suitable affine opens, and choose a coordinate of a local point outside k. Proposition17 gives a contradiction. The printed blanket parabolic reduction has the explicit /77 counterexample; the general-curve proof remains a checkpoint gap until that branch is repaired.

items.name: Countable open-lifting implies birational lifting
items.statement: For a curve over a countable field, if S_V/k→S_U/k is surjective for every pair of nonempty opens V⊆U⊆X, then every section of every U is b.l.
items.note: Countability gives a cofinal sequence and compatible choices; this is not the assertion that arbitrary inverse systems of nonempty sets have nonempty limit.

items.name: Birational lifting implies all open-lifting maps surjective
items.statement: For a curve over a countable field, if every section of every nonempty open U⊆X is b.l., then every S_V/k→S_U/k is surjective.
items.note: This direction does not need countability; restrict a function-field lift to V.

items.name: Sections of the function field as an inverse limit
items.statement: S_k(X)/k identifies with the inverse limit of S_U/k over nonempty opens U⊆X in the source’s section topology/conjugacy convention.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 23 and Lemma 26, [20] Lemma 259
items.note: Generic cover descent alone does not justify interchanging quotient and inverse limit; use the actual section-space result.

items.name: Cuspidalization equivalence
items.statement: The global cuspidalization conjecture is equivalent to every Galois section of every hyperbolic curve over every field finitely generated over Q being b.l.
items.note: Uses countability and quantification over all opens.

items.name: Theorem B equivalence for all finitely generated extensions
items.statement: For hyperbolic X/k with k finitely generated over Q, the following are equivalent: (i) for every finitely generated K/k every section of X_K is geometric or cuspidal; (ii) for every such K every section of X_K is b.l.
items.note: Apply (ii) at K(t) to get t-b.l. over K; omitting the extension quantifier invalidates the argument.

items.name: Section and cuspidalization conjectures are equivalent
items.statement: The global section conjecture is equivalent to the global cuspidalization conjecture.
items.locator: Published paper Theorem B consequence p.147
items.note: An equivalence of conjectures is proved; neither conjecture is asserted true.

items.name: Hilbertian fields and thin subsets
items.statement: Use Hilbertian fields and thin sets in the sense required for finite étale covers of nonempty opens V⊆A1: the image of a connected cover of degree>1 is thin, finite unions are thin and V(k) is not thin.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Test a degree-one cover and a nonsplit quadratic cover; import the general field/irreducibility owner.

items.name: Hilbertian finite-cover section criterion
items.statement: If k is Hilbertian, V⊆A1 is nonempty open and W→V is finite étale with W(k)→V(k) surjective, then W→V has a section.
items.note: A finite union of thin images cannot cover V(k); some connected component has degree one.

items.name: Relative section isomorphism torsor
items.statement: If Π_X/V=lim_i Φ_i with Φ_i proper étale gerbes and s1,s2 sections, then Isom(s1,s2)=lim_i(V×_(Φ_i)V); each finite-stage fiber product is finite étale over V.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Use 2-fiber products along s1,s2; test identical sections and a nontrivial finite torsor.

items.name: Compact inverse-limit nonemptiness
items.statement: A cofiltered inverse system of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces has nonempty limit; in particular this holds for finite nonempty sets with discrete topology.
items.note: Pinned theorem read; its use on the finite sets of sections Isom_i(V) is valid.

items.name: Hilbertian specialization determines a section
items.statement: Let k be Hilbertian, V⊆A1 nonempty open and X→V a family of curves. Two relative fundamental-gerbe sections with isomorphic specializations at every v∈V(k) are isomorphic.
items.note: Gerbe proof uses finite étale isomorphism covers and compactness. Group proof uses nonthin geometric sections and finite-kernel conjugators. No statement for an arbitrary base with too few rational points.

items.name: Nonthin geometric sections generate π1
items.statement: For a nonthin S⊆V(k), chosen geometric section images r_v(Gal(k)), v∈S, topologically generate π1(V).
items.note: An open subgroup containing all images would define a connected cover whose image contains S; Hilbert irreducibility forces degree one.

items.name: Finite-kernel approximations of the family extension
items.statement: Write π1(X) as the inverse limit of extensions G_i→π1(V) with finite kernels H_i obtained by pulling finite quotients back along π1(V); π1(F)=lim_i H_i.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 25 group proof pp.147–148
items.note: Planning API and tests: Use image of N_i in π1(V) when writing the quotient; compare conjugators at all finite stages.

items.name: Cuspidal packet injectivity and distinctness
items.statement: Let U/k be a smooth hyperbolic curve in characteristic zero. Assume injectivity of the section map for proper genus≥2 curves over finite extensions of k. Then a cuspidal section determines its cusp uniquely, the local packet map is injective, and cuspidal and geometric sections are disjoint.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 26 and Theorem C cite [19] Theorem 17(2)
items.note: Read author 2012 PDF p.8 Theorem17(1)–(3). The published proof’s uniqueness-of-cusp citation is part (1); part (2) controls the packet. Retain the proper injectivity hypothesis.

items.name: Birational-conjecture reformulation
items.statement: The birational section conjecture over fields finitely generated over Q is equivalent to every b.l. section of every curve over those fields being geometric or cuspidal.
items.note: Correct compressed proof wording: images on opens containing the associated rational point can be GEOMETRIC. Pass to the cofinal opens omitting that point before using cuspidal packets and their inverse limit.

items.name: Number-field reduction for the ordinary birational conjecture
items.statement: If the birational section conjecture holds for curves over all number fields, it holds over all fields finitely generated over Q.
items.locator: Published paper §1 p.130; Theorem C p.149, [17] Theorem C
items.note: Saïdi–Tyler arXiv:1909.12099v3 pp.1–5 read, TheoremC on p.4: the all-number-field hypothesis implies the all-finitely-generated-field conclusion without a Shafarevich–Tate finiteness hypothesis. The words geometric birational section there mean Bresciani’s cuspidal birational section. Do not import the conditional TheoremsA/B instead.

items.name: Theorem C forward direction
items.statement: Assume the birational section conjecture. For every number field k, z∈S_k(P1)/k and nonempty open U⊆P1, there is nonempty open V⊆U and a π1 section r of (U×V)\Δ→V with r_v=ι_(U\{v})(z) for every v∈V(k).
items.note: If the rational point p associated to z is in U use V=U\{p} and its graph. If p is a cusp use packet injectivity, constant loops and extension over U.

items.name: Theorem C reverse direction
items.statement: If the diagonal-family lifting assertion in the preceding item holds for every number field, every birational P1 section and every nonempty open U, then the birational section conjecture holds over all fields finitely generated over Q.
items.note: Use Saïdi–Tyler, the coordinate reduction and Lemma25 to make all open lifts compatible, then Proposition17.

items.name: Uniqueness and compatibility of diagonal-family lifts
items.statement: For fixed k,z,U,V in Theorem C with V affine, at most one relative π1 section has the prescribed specializations; shrinking U,V gives compatible sections after common restriction.
items.locator: Published paper §1 p.132; Theorem C p.149
items.note: Lemma25 also identifies its image in U×V with the constant base-change section. For P1 itself first shrink V to an affine open.

items.name: Geometric and cuspidal lift through the diagonal complement
items.statement: A point p∈U(k) gives a geometric section of (U×(U\{p}))\Δ; if p∈(P1\U)(k), its cuspidal packet restricts compatibly along U\{v} for every v∈U(k).
items.note: Do not equate packets to singletons: uniqueness is of the lift of the SPECIFIED packet section.

items.name: Schmidt’s actual Brauer–Severi input
items.statement: Over characteristic-zero k, if X is a Brauer–Severi variety and U is an open subvariety of the complement of a twisted hyperplane arrangement which admits a homotopy rational point, then X splits and U has a k-rational point.
items.locator: Schmidt arXiv:1503.08108v1, TheoremA p.2; invoked at Bresciani p.141
items.note: Source statement read. A section and a homotopy rational point agree in the K(π,1) affine-curve case. Splitting X says nothing about every boundary component being rational; /77 therefore remains unresolved.

items.name: Semiabelian scheme
items.statement: A semiabelian scheme is an extension of an abelian scheme by a torus, with its exact sequence and base change retained.
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma8 p.138; generic carrier supplier
items.note: Planning API and tests: toric/abelian projections, base change and split product; compare T=0 and A=0. Use the existing general owner, before the curve-specific generalized Jacobian.

items.name: Mattuck torsion consequence
items.statement: For a finite extension K/Qp and an abelian variety A/K, the subgroup of torsion elements in A(K) is finite.
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma8 p.138; Mattuck Theorem7 p.114
items.note: The open subgroup furnished by /62 is torsion-free and finite index; restriction of the quotient map to torsion is injective.
proofSteps: The torsion subgroup intersects U trivially since the additive group O_K^g is torsion-free.
Its injection into the finite quotient A(K)/U proves finiteness; the order of a finite quotient need not equal the torsion order.

items.name: Profinite-completion universal property
items.statement: For abstract G and profinite P in the same universe, continuous homomorphisms hat G→P correspond to group homomorphisms G→P; equality is detected on the dense unit image.
items.locator: Replacement proof of /29; completion carrier supplier
items.note: Entire source file read. Reuse Mathlib's profinite completion, not the different power-quotient completion /18. The same-universe convention is retained.

items.name: Finitely many open subgroups of each positive index
items.statement: In a topologically finitely generated topological group G, the type of open subgroups of any fixed nonzero index n is finite. Compactness is not required for n≠0.
items.locator: Bekka CorollaryC proof p.15; existing positive-index theorem
items.note: Statement and full proof read. Give the abstract finitely generated N the discrete topology and apply /138; every subgroup is open. Do not use the later compact-only theorem or n=0 (Lean index zero means infinite index).

items.name: Abstract finite generation implies topological finite generation
items.statement: A finitely generated group is topologically finitely generated in every group topology, in particular its discrete topology.
items.note: Statement/proof read. This implication is not reversible for a profinite topology; Zhat is a counterexample to interpreting topological generators as abstract generators.

items.name: Finite intersections preserve finite index
items.statement: The intersection of a finite family of finite-index subgroups of a group has finite index.
items.note: Statement/proof read. Applies to the finite type of index-n subgroups from /137; no normality or finite generation is needed for this intersection lemma.

items.name: Characteristic finite-index core
items.statement: For finitely generated N and finite-index K≤N of index n>0, define C_n as the intersection of all subgroups of index n. Then C_n≤K, C_n is characteristic (hence normal), and C_n has finite index.
items.locator: Bekka arXiv:2305.04803v1 §4.1 p.15; direct group-theoretic proof
items.note: API: membership iff membership in every index-n subgroup; characteristicity under each automorphism; inclusion in K; finite-index instance from /137–/139. Tests: n=1 gives N; N=Z,n=6 gives 6Z; N=S3,n=3 gives 1 despite the chosen order-two K being nonnormal. Do not assert endomorphism invariance: characteristic is automorphism invariance.

items.name: Finite quotient of a split extension detecting the kernel
items.statement: For an action H→Aut(N) and finite-index characteristic C≤N, let Q_C be the finite image of H in Aut(N/C). The map N⋊H→(N/C)⋊Q_C sends (n,h) to (n mod C, action(h)); it is surjective and its restriction to N has kernel C.
items.locator: Direct finite-quotient proof of /29; Bekka CorollaryC corroborates the endpoint
items.note: API: action descent, quotient homomorphism, multiplication formula, kernel on N, projection to Q_C, compatibility under characteristic refinements. Tests: trivial action yields N/C; inversion of Z gives finite dihedral quotients for modulus≥3; swapping coordinates of (Z/2)^2 does not descend through a chosen non-invariant index-two subgroup. No claim that all N-subgroups are H-stable.

items.name: Full induced profinite topology on a finitely generated split kernel
items.statement: For finitely generated N and G=N⋊H with H arbitrary, the restrictions to N of finite-index normal subgroups of G are cofinal among finite-index normal subgroups of N. Hence hat N→hat G is injective and a topological embedding.
items.locator: Direct proof from /140–/141 and finite-quotient coordinates; Bresciani Lemma1 application
items.note: For any finite-index K≤N choose C_n≤K and use ker of /141. Separate two points of hat N by a coordinate N/K and then the extending finite quotient. Compact-to-Hausdorff injectivity supplies the embedding. N itself need not be residually finite.

items.name: Right exactness of profinite completion
items.statement: For a normal subgroup N of any abstract group G, hat G divided by the closure of the unit image of N is canonically the profinite completion of G/N. In particular hat G→hat(G/N) is surjective and its kernel equals the image of hat N.
items.locator: Bekka arXiv:2305.04803v1 Proposition6(ii), pp.9–10, complete proof read
items.note: Use existing closed-normal profinite quotient, /136's universal property, and compactness: image(hat N)=closure(image N). No injectivity of hat N is asserted. The v1 proof says Bohr compactification once in the profinite argument, a typographical mismatch; its universal-property argument is profinite.

items.name: Completion preserves split extensions with finitely generated kernel
items.statement: For arbitrary abstract H, finitely generated N and an action H→Aut(N), completing 1→N→N⋊H→H→1 gives a split exact sequence of profinite groups. The extended splitting induces a continuous action of hat H on hat N and a topological group isomorphism hat(N⋊H)≃hat N⋊hat H.
items.locator: Bekka arXiv:2305.04803v1 CorollaryC p.4 and §4.1 p.15; self-contained replacement proof here
items.note: Combine /142 and /143, and extend the original splitting by /136. Define the completed action by conjugation inside hat G using the closed-kernel embedding; continuity follows from this construction, not an unspecified topology on Aut(hat N). Prove multiplication-map inverse and naturality for maps preserving splittings. Tests: finite N,H; trivial action; Z⋊C2 inversion. No goodness, residual finiteness, or finite generation of H is assumed.

items.name: An abstract extension with free quotient splits
items.statement: If G→F(S) is a surjective homomorphism to a free abstract group, it admits a homomorphic section: choose a lift of each free generator and extend by the free-group universal property.
items.locator: Direct replacement proof for Bresciani Lemma1 p.134
items.note: Use Mathlib's existing FreeGroup carrier/lift; no new free profinite group is needed. The chosen section need not arise from a map of curves. Empty S gives the trivial quotient; S singleton gives a split extension by Z. Combine with /144 only after identifying the kernel as finitely generated.

items.name: Finite generation cannot be dropped from split completion
items.statement: Let N=⊕_(j∈Z) C2 and let Z act by shifting the coordinates. The split inclusion N→N⋊Z does not induce an injection on profinite completions.
items.locator: Direct counterexample accompanying replacement proof; not claimed as Bresciani's statement
items.note: Let K be the kernel of the coordinate-zero character N→C2. In any finite quotient of N⋊Z the shift has some order t≥1, forcing e_0 and e_t to have the same image. Thus e_0+e_t lies in the restriction kernel but not K. The full profinite topology on N is not induced; an injective hat N→hat G would be a compact-to-Hausdorff embedding and would induce that topology, contradiction. The inclusion of the abstract groups remains injective; do not confuse it with completion injectivity.

items.name: Canonical locally-full/faithful factorization of affine gerbes
items.statement: Every morphism Γ→Δ of affine gerbes factors canonically as Γ→Δ′→Δ with first map locally full and second faithful.
items.locator: Borne–Vistoli2019 Proposition3.9, published pp.539–540; full proof read
items.note: Rigidify by the kernels of automorphism maps, form the fpqc quotient groupoid, and verify affine descent. This does not assume neutralization over k. Import the existing fpqc stack framework /19–/22. Test BG→BH via the image subgroup.

items.name: Locally full morphisms detected on a cofiltered target presentation
items.statement: For a cofiltered system of affine gerbes Δ_i and f:Γ→lim_i Δ_i, if every composite Γ→Δ_i is locally full, then f is locally full.
items.locator: Borne–Vistoli2019 Proposition3.11, published pp.540–541; proof read
items.note: Choose a field-valued object of Γ. Faithful flatness of affine group maps over a field is injectivity of the coordinate Hopf-algebra map. Each level map is injective, hence so is its filtered colimit. The statement requires the compatible morphism to the limit, not independently chosen maps.

items.name: Finite étale gerbe presentation with locally full projections
items.statement: A profinite étale gerbe admits a cofiltered finite étale presentation whose projections and transition maps are locally full, obtained by replacing each finite stage with the canonical image of the projection.
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma2 p.135; Borne–Vistoli2019 Proposition3.9 plus direct cofinal-image refinement
items.note: API: finite-stage image, transition factorization, comparison with original limit, invariance under refinement, locally full projections. After a common fpqc neutralizing field extension this is replacement of finite groups by the images of the profinite group; the two limits agree because every compatible tuple already lies in those images. Descend the canonical factorizations. Tests: a system with non-surjective transitions; a constant finite gerbe; a neutral infinite profinite group. The proper relative-gerbe conclusion is /35, not a second assertion bundled here.

items.name: Geometric Albanese comparison for smooth curves
items.statement: For a smooth connected curve X over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, the generalized Albanese map induces π1(X)^ab≃TJ, with J the generalized Jacobian. For a smooth proper compactification C and reduced boundary D, the obstruction is dual to the torsion of NS(C)/⟨[d]:d∈D⟩. This vanishes: NS(C)≃Z by degree, and the quotient is Z when D is empty and zero when D is nonempty. All finite étale covers are tame in this characteristic.
items.locator: Spieß–Szamuely, math/0009017, §4, Propositions 4.1 and 4.3, author pp.8–10 (Harari–Szamuely Remark 2.4 cites published Proposition 4.4)
items.note: Read both propositions and their proofs in the arXiv PDF. This is the curve specialization of their exact sequence, not an isomorphism for arbitrary varieties. The cited Picard 1-motive/Serre-duality machinery remains a prerequisite of its supplier blueprint. Tests: proper genus g gives Zhat^(2g), Gm gives Zhat(1), and three punctures on P1 give Zhat(1)^2.

items.name: Canonical Tate-module band of a semiabelian torsor
items.statement: For a semiabelian variety J over a characteristic-zero field k and a J-torsor P, let Ψ_n be the gerbe of liftings of P along [n]:J→J. The compatible tautological maps P→Ψ_n identify Π_P/k with lim_n Ψ_n, canonically banded by TJ=lim_n J[n]. The transition maps use divisibility and multiplication on torsion. The band is independent of a splitting point of P.
items.locator: Bresciani, Essential dimension and pro-finite group schemes, arXiv:1904.00789v2, Lemma 5.8 and proof, pp.19–20; Harari–Szamuely §2 and Remark 2.4
items.note: Proof read: form the Kummer lifting gerbes, use the tautological trivialization over P, and check equivalence after a splitting field. The final word A in the proof of Lemma 5.8 must read TA; its statement already gives the correct band. SourceIssue E7 records this dependency misprint. No assertion that neutral Π_P implies P(k)≠∅.

items.name: Neutralization of a banded gerbe by a chosen object
items.statement: For an fpqc gerbe G over k with a chosen object s∈G(k), the functor x↦Isom(s,x) is an equivalence G≃B_k Aut(s), taking s to the trivial torsor. If G has a commutative band H, Aut(s) identifies with H and changing s does not change this band. A morphism of gerbes together with the image of the chosen object induces the corresponding homomorphism of automorphism group sheaves (group schemes when representable).
items.locator: Bresciani, published §2 p.133 and Lemma 8 p.138; Bresciani 1904.00789v2 Lemma 5.8 for the Tate-module band
items.note: Elementary descent proof in the report: Isom is locally a simply transitive automorphism torsor; twisting s constructs the inverse, with descent for objects and arrows. Use fpqc torsors for profinite H. Test the trivial torsor, twisting by an H-torsor, and the independence of inner conjugation only for a commutative band. Owned by SF.1.

items.name: Contraction fixed point on a complete subset
items.statement: For a complete subset S of an extended metric space, a self-map preserving S and contracting there with constant c<1 has a fixed point in the finite-distance component of any starting point x∈S with finite distance to f(x). Its iterates converge with the stated geometric error bound.

items.name: Local inverse from an invertible strict derivative
items.statement: For normed spaces over a nontrivially normed field, with complete domain, an invertible strict Fréchet derivative of f at a supplies an open partial homeomorphism with underlying function f and a in its source.

api.name: Bresciani24.n154.map
api.statement: The forward function is the original f.

api.name: Bresciani24.n154.inverse
api.statement: On the chosen source/target, inverse composition is identity.

api.name: Bresciani24.n154.neighborhood
api.statement: The source is an open neighborhood of a, and the target of f(a).

tests.name: Bresciani24.n154.identity
tests.statement: For f=id and derivative id, the local map is identity on its domain.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n154.p_scaling
tests.statement: On K/Qp finite, multiplication by p has an invertible K-linear derivative and local inverse x↦x/p.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n154.zero_derivative
tests.statement: The map x↦x² at 0 does not meet the derivative hypothesis.

uses.how: Supplies the topological local inverse in the smooth-point chart; analytic inverse is a separate supplier.

items.name: Restricted multivariable analytic functions on a closed ball
items.statement: For finite K/Qp and a radius r in |K×|, use the Banach algebra of restricted power series on the closed maximum-norm ball B_r⊂K^d. The norm is the weighted supremum of coefficients. Substitution by maps taking a ball into a smaller ball is admitted with the Gauss-norm bound; a Gauss-norm Cauchy sequence has an analytic limit.
items.locator: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0; Mattuck pp.93–97, addition/multiplication/substitution and inversion

api.name: Bresciani24.n155.gauss
api.statement: For f=Σa_αX^α, the norm is sup |a_α|r^|α|, with weighted coefficients tending to zero.

api.name: Bresciani24.n155.restrict
api.statement: Restriction to a smaller radius is a continuous algebra map and respects composition.

api.name: Bresciani24.n155.limit
api.statement: Convergence in the Gauss norm gives a restricted series and uniform convergence of its evaluations.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n155.polynomial
tests.statement: The norm of X_i on B_r is r.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n155.vector
tests.statement: Use the maximum of component norms for K^d-valued maps.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n155.pointwise
tests.statement: Pointwise or bare uniform convergence is not substituted for convergence in the analytic Banach norm.

uses.how: Completes the logarithm sequence as an analytic function.

items.name: Smooth algebraic points have analytic coordinates
items.statement: For finite K/Qp, a smooth finite-type K-scheme X and x∈X(K), a neighborhood of x in X(K) is a K-analytic manifold of dimension dim_x X. Algebraic morphisms between smooth schemes induce analytic maps in these charts, with the algebraic tangent derivative.
items.locator: Mattuck implicit/inversion theorem pp.97–98; existing Howe–Klevdal /179 classical-point interface
proofSteps: Choose a standard smooth affine presentation at x with an invertible Jacobian minor. Separate free coordinates and equation coordinates.

Solve the polynomial equations by the nonarchimedean analytic implicit-function theorem; the pinned inverse-function theorem supplies the underlying open partial homeomorphism. Analytic inverse and polynomial-to-manifold compatibility remain precise supplier obligations, not consequences of the name alone.
Regular maps are rational expressions with denominators nonzero near x, hence analytic on a smaller ball; the chain rule gives the tangent comparison.

items.name: Small commutative analytic group law
items.statement: In coordinates centered at the identity of a finite-dimensional commutative K-analytic group, its multiplication is a convergent vector series F(X,Y)=X+Y+terms of degree at least two, its inverse is −X+terms of degree at least two, and its multiplication-by-p series P(X) has linear term pX. On a sufficiently small closed ball, multiplication and inverse preserve the ball.
items.locator: Local analytic replacement for Mattuck Theorem7; existing Caro–Pasten formal-n and multiplication-linear interfaces

api.name: Bresciani24.n157.laws
api.statement: Export identity, inverse, commutativity and associativity on the chosen common domain.

api.name: Bresciani24.n157.multiplication
api.statement: P is the p-fold sum in F, P(0)=0 and its derivative is p·id.

api.name: Bresciani24.n157.shrink
api.statement: Restrict the same germ to a smaller invariant ball; the group laws and coordinate changes agree there.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n157.additive
tests.statement: F=X+Y has P=pX and no remainder.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n157.multiplicative
tests.statement: In the coordinate x=u−1, F=x+y+xy and P=(1+x)^p−1.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n157.noncommutative
tests.statement: The power map need not be a homomorphism in a noncommutative group; that setting is excluded.

uses.how: Provides the analytic remainders to bound.

items.name: Quantitative small-ball bounds
items.statement: For F and P of /157, choose C>0 and r>0 in |K×| with ε=Cr/|p|<1. On B_r, R=P−p·id satisfies |R(x)|≤C|x|² and |R(x)−R(y)|≤Cr|x−y|; on every B_s with s≤r the latter bound is Cs. F−(X+Y) has the corresponding quadratic bound. Consequently |P(x)−P(y)|=|p||x−y|.
items.locator: Explicit coefficient estimate in the continuation, from the convergent-series operations of Mattuck pp.93–97
proofSteps: Take a smaller radius inside a common convergence ball. The coefficients of all degree≥2 remainders are bounded by C times the radius weight of degree−2.
Factor the difference of each monomial as a telescoping sum. The ultrametric inequality bounds it by s^(degree−1)|x−y| on B_s; the same coefficient majorant gives Cs.

Shrink r until Cr<|p|. The linear term then strictly dominates the difference remainder, giving equality of norms. Bounds on multiplication and inverse make B_r a subgroup. No good-reduction or p>2 hypothesis occurs.

items.name: Logarithm as normalized multiplication iterates
items.statement: Under /158 define L_n(x)=p^(−n)P^[n](x), where P^[n] is n-fold composition. The sequence converges in the Gauss norm on B_r to L, with L(0)=0, derivative id, and |L_(n+1)(x)−L_n(x)|≤C|p|^(n−1)|x|².
items.locator: Explicit replacement proof for the finite-K/Qp case of Mattuck Theorem7
proofSteps: Induction using /158 gives |P^[n](x)|=|p|^n|x| and the same shrinking-ball bounds in the Gauss norm.
Write L_(n+1)−L_n=p^(−n−1)R(P^[n](x)); its bound is C|p|^(n−1)|x|². The Gauss bounds tend to zero, so their telescoping sum converges in the complete ultrametric Banach algebra /155.
The constant term remains zero and the linear term remains identity at every level and in the coefficient limit.

api.name: Bresciani24.n159.normalization
api.statement: L(0)=0 and the derivative at 0 is identity.

api.name: Bresciani24.n159.restrict
api.statement: The same normalized limit restricts to every smaller admissible ball; it is independent of the radius after restriction.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n159.additive
tests.statement: For P=pX every L_n and L equal id.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n159.multiplicative
tests.statement: For F=x+y+xy the limit is log(1+x) on a sufficiently small ball.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n159.two_adic_boundary
tests.statement: At p=2, x=−2 corresponds to the torsion unit −1. The too-large ball 2Z2 cannot support an injective logarithm; 4Z2 is an admissible smaller ball.

uses.how: Supplies the limit whose group law is proved.

items.name: The normalized limit is a group homomorphism
items.statement: On B_r with F as above, L(F(x,y))=L(x)+L(y).
items.locator: Continuation proof, local form of Mattuck Theorem7
proofSteps: Since F is commutative, P^[n](F(x,y))=F(P^[n](x),P^[n](y)).
Divide by p^n. The difference from L_n(x)+L_n(y) has norm at most C|p|^n max(|x|,|y|)^2, which tends to zero. Pass to the limit.

items.name: The logarithm is an isometry near identity
items.statement: For L of /159 and ε=Cr/|p|<1, h=L−id is ε-Lipschitz on B_r. Hence |L(x)−L(y)|=|x−y|, and L is injective.
proofSteps: The n-th telescoping difference has Lipschitz constant at most C r |p|^(n−1), using /158 on B_(|p|^n r) and the exact contraction of P^[n].
The ultrametric sum is bounded by the maximum constant ε; its limit h has the same bound. Since ε<1, the identity term strictly dominates for x≠y.

items.name: The small logarithm maps onto the full coordinate ball
items.statement: For each y∈B_r, x↦y−(L(x)−x) preserves B_r and contracts with constant ε<1. Its unique fixed point solves L(x)=y. Thus L is a homeomorphic group isomorphism from (B_r,F) onto (B_r,+).
items.locator: Continuation proof using the pinned contraction theorem
proofSteps: h(0)=0 and |h(x)|≤ε|x| ensure the self-map remains in B_r. The ball is complete.
Apply /153, then use /161 for uniqueness and continuity of the inverse. The inverse is an isometry as well.

items.name: Analytic inverse of the small logarithm
items.statement: The inverse of /162 is analytic, with identity derivative, so L is an analytic group isomorphism. Its germ agrees with the normalized characteristic-zero formal logarithm already owned by the FormalLieTheory continuation.
items.locator: Mattuck inversion theorem pp.97–98; Gauss-norm inverse iteration in this continuation
proofSteps: Solve X=Y−h(X) by iteration in the vector Tate algebra on B_r. The coefficient telescoping estimate giving ε-Lipschitzness holds in its Gauss norm, so substitution is a contraction on the radius-r ball of series.
Completeness /155 gives a convergent analytic inverse series; evaluations are the unique fixed points of /162.

The derivative is id. For two normalized formal logarithms, compose with one inverse; an additive formal map in characteristic zero is linear, by comparing the mixed coefficients in H(X+Y)=H(X)+H(Y). Its identity derivative forces equality. This comparison does not import Caro–Pasten’s large-prime full-disc theorem.

items.name: Open additive subgroup of local abelian-variety points
items.statement: For finite K/Qp and an abelian variety A/K of dimension g, choose the identity chart /156 and a ball as above. Its inverse image U⊂A(K) is an open subgroup analytically isomorphic to (B_r,+), hence after scalar rescaling to (O_K^g,+).
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma8; Mattuck Theorem7, finite-K/Qp specialization

api.name: Bresciani24.n164.subgroup
api.statement: The chosen chart intertwines the group law on U and vector addition under L.

api.name: Bresciani24.n164.rank
api.statement: Choosing r=|a| identifies B_r=aO_K^g and multiplication by a^−1 identifies it with O_K^g.

api.name: Bresciani24.n164.smallness
api.statement: Smaller admissible balls give nested open torsion-free subgroups; no canonical radius is asserted.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n164.dimension_zero
tests.statement: For the zero abelian variety, U and O_K^0 are the trivial group.
