tests.name: Bresciani24.n164.bad_reduction
tests.statement: The construction uses smoothness over K and works for an elliptic curve with bad reduction.

tests.name: Bresciani24.n164.two
tests.statement: At p=2 shrink the radius; there is no claim that the entire first residue disc is torsion-free.

uses.how: Supplies the local subgroup in Mattuck’s input.

items.name: Compactness of projective local points
items.statement: For finite K/Qp and a projective K-scheme X, X(K) with its usual K-adic topology is compact Hausdorff.
items.locator: Mattuck compactness step pp.113,117; explicit normalized-coordinate proof
proofSteps: For P^N(K), normalize a nonzero coordinate vector by a coordinate of maximal absolute value. The finitely many charts with that coordinate equal to 1 are continuous images of compact O_K^N. They cover P^N(K).
A projective closed subscheme has a closed zero locus in P^N(K), so its K-points are compact. The affine-chart topology is Hausdorff and agrees with /156.
Compactness of O_K and the chart topology are imported from the existing local-field and analytic-point suppliers. Compactness is not inferred merely from the word proper in the algebraic carrier.

items.name: Projectivity of an abelian variety over a field
items.statement: An abelian variety over a characteristic-zero field is projective and has a symmetric ample line bundle. This is a field theorem; it does not assert projectivity or an ample line bundle for an arbitrary abelian scheme over an arbitrary base.
items.locator: Milne, Abelian Varieties, author revision 2022-01-02, Theorem7.1 and Corollary7.2, pp.10–12
proofSteps: Over an algebraic closure choose finitely many divisors separating the identity from other points and nonzero tangent directions. The theorem of the square makes suitable translates linearly equivalent to three times their sum, separating all points and tangent directions.
Over a characteristic-zero field the divisors descend to a finite Galois extension; the sum of conjugates is ample and descends. Very ampleness is detected after field extension.

Tensor an ample line bundle with its inverse-pullback under [−1] to make it symmetric. The theorem of the square, Cartier descent and very-ampleness criteria are explicit algebraic supplier leaves, recorded as a gap until decomposed.

items.name: Bounded local torsion kills the inverse Tate invariants
items.statement: For finite K/Qp and A/K, (TA)^G_K=lim_n A[n](K)=0, where the divisibility transition A[mn]→A[n] is multiplication by m.
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma8 p.138; explicit bounded-exponent proof
proofSteps: Choose N annihilating the finite group A(K)_tors. For a compatible family a_n, a_n=N a_(Nn)=0 for every n.
Invariants commute with this inverse limit coordinatewise. The assertion uses the common bound N, not just finiteness of each A[n](K).

items.name: Direct cocycle proof of the local H1 injection
items.statement: For the exact compact G_K-modules 0→TT→TJ→TA→0 supplied by /57, the vanishing /167 gives injectivity H1_cont(K,TT)→H1_cont(K,TJ).
proofSteps: Represent a class killed in H1(K,TJ) by a continuous TT-valued cocycle c with c(σ)=σj−j for some j∈TJ.

The image of j in TA is invariant and therefore zero by /167. Exactness places j in TT, proving c is already a TT-coboundary. No passage from termwise long exact sequences through an unchecked derived limit is used.

routes.title: Anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty, Part II: birational lifting and Galois-section specialization
routes.brief:
Extend Anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty), separately from the Betts–Stix p-adic-period-mapping extension. Own birational/t-birational/quasi-t-birational section conditions, ramified specializing loops and the three proved endpoints of Bresciani, Invent. math.235 (2024),129–150. For X/k smooth geometrically connected and k finitely generated over Q prove: a section is geometric or cuspidal iff its base change to k(t) lifts birationally (Theorem A). For fixed hyperbolic X/k prove equivalence of geometric-or-cuspidal and birational lifting AFTER EVERY finitely generated extension K/k (Theorem B), and deduce the equivalence, not truth, of the global section and cuspidalization conjectures. Prove Theorem C exactly: the ordinary birational section conjecture is equivalent to existence, for every number field k, birational section z of k(P1)/k and nonempty open U⊆P1, of a nonempty open V⊆U and relative π1 section of (U×V)\Δ→V whose v-specialization is the prescribed image of z on U\{v} for every v∈V(k).

Build Lemmas1–26 and their proof leaves in source order, with generic foundation ownership below, then Proposition17's stronger pro-open diagonal lifting criterion and its completed-unit valuation proof, the number-field open-lifting Lemma16, quasi-t-b.l. reduction, Tamagawa neighborhoods and the coherence input. Do not substitute the rational-function field for Spec k(y)×k Spec k(t) with the diagonal deleted. Track restricted completed products, nonrational closed points, finite places, residue characteristic zero and the nonparabolic reductions. A specialization is an essential-image class and need not be unique; the C[x]_(x), z=x example must reject the converse to constant-loop⇒unique specialization. For Hilbertian uniqueness keep finite-kernel conjugacy limits, not arbitrary choices of conjugators.

Import path torsors/sections from the parent NC.0; finite covers, homotopy exactness and relative fundamental gerbes from Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0–IG.2); gerbes, root stacks, tame valuative criteria and extension gluing from Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1), with local curve geometry from SF.3; compact cohomology/Kummer completions from Global Galois duality and compact coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1); generalized Jacobians/Albanese torsors from the proposed JacobianChallenge Part II; local torsion from the proposed AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli Part II. routes.title: Profinite and pro-p groups, Part II: exactness of completion for split extensions
routes.brief:
Take Profinite and pro-p groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups) as FIRST prerequisite, importing its Layer0 completion and quotient infrastructure and Layer3 topological-generation substrate. Do not rebuild those carriers or their already-implemented universal properties. The new endpoint is: for an abstract split extension 1→N→G→H→1 with N finitely generated and H arbitrary, its profinite completion is split exact, and hat G is isomorphic as a topological group to hat N⋊hat H with the action induced by the chosen splitting. Bekka, On Bohr compactifications and profinite completions of group extensions, arXiv:2305.04803v1, CorollaryC, independently states this endpoint; use the direct finite-quotient proof detailed in the paper report rather than importing his representation-theoretic TheoremB as an unexplained hypothesis.

First reuse TauCeti.isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated_of_fg and the nonzero-index form of finite_openSubgroup_index_eq, applied with discrete topology. Define C_n as the intersection of all index-n subgroups of N, prove finite index using Mathlib.Subgroup.finiteIndex_iInf, and prove characteristicity and C_n≤K for a given index-n K. Descend H's action to N/C_n, take its finite image Q_n in Aut(N/C_n), and construct the surjective finite quotient G→(N/C_n)⋊Q_n whose kernel restricts to C_n. Deduce the cofinal restriction property and injectivity/topological embedding of hat N→hat G. Separately prove general right exactness by identifying hat G/closure(N) with hat(G/N) through the existing universal property. Extend the abstract splitting to hat H, construct the completed action by conjugation, and prove the canonical semidirect-product comparison and its naturality for maps preserving the chosen splittings. No residual-finiteness, cohomological goodness or finite generation of H is a hypothesis.

Add the free-quotient splitting lemma using the existing abstract FreeGroup universal property. Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.1) imports it with the separate curve-topology/Riemann-existence input: smooth affine complex curves have free fundamental group and curve fibers have finitely generated fundamental group. This geometric application is owned there, never by this generic Part II. Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) likewise owns gerbes, not this roadmap. Profinite arithmetic (ProfiniteArithmetic) owns profinite powers and topological Aut/Out carriers; the present action is built via the closed-kernel comparison and does not construct another Aut topology.

Tests include finite groups, trivial action, all small dihedral quotients of Z⋊C2, a non-invariant index-two subgroup under coordinate swap, and the sharp negative split example (⊕_Z C2)⋊Z: coordinate-zero kernel cannot contain any restricted finite-quotient kernel, because a finite-order shift identifies e_0 and e_t. Thus finite generation cannot simply be deleted. Distinguish ordinary profinite completion from the paper's power-quotient completion of an arbitrary abelian group. Every construction has projection, multiplication, kernel, refinement, naturality and concrete unit-test obligations. No blanket left exactness of profinite completion, general goodness theorem, pro-p replacement, or geometric section of a curve family is claimed.
